title: Metric stitching router for LLM inference KPIs
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem:
The serving runtime, API gateway, and cache subsystems each emit metrics with divergent label schemas and different aggregation boundaries. This fragmentation prevents reliable derivation of production KPIs (effective tokens/sec, end-to-end tail latency, KV-cache hit-adjusted latency) and inflates cardinality in Prometheus, causing increased storage costs and noisy dashboards.

Goal:
Implement a lightweight "metric stitching router" that sits between OTel collectors and Prometheus remote_write endpoints to unify label schemas, compute derived inference KPIs at ingestion, and apply cardinality controls and exemplar forwarding. The router should preserve low latency for SLO-critical signals and be deployable as a horizontally scalable stateless service with local aggregation sharding.

Non-functional requirements:
- Handle sustained ingest of 250k metric points/sec with spikes to 1M/sec in peak tests.
- Bounded memory per instance and backpressure to collectors if overwhelmed.
- 99.9% availability for pipeline ingestion; no single-point-of-failure.
- Derived KPIs computed with <500ms processing lag for 95% of points.
- Configurable relabeling rules and derived KPI formulas via central config (Console + GitOps).

Signals to produce (examples):
- inference_tokens_effective_per_second (derived, per-model, per-region)
- effective_batching_rate (derived: tokens_generated / request_count)
- kv_cache_hit_rate (ratio with exemplars to traces)
- e2e_p95_latency_ms (stitching gateway latency + runtime latency)
- model_variant_fallback_rate (counter)
Integration expectations:
- Accept OTel metrics via OTLP/gRPC and Prometheus remote_write for legacy collectors.
- Emit to Prometheus remote_write with histogram buckets + exemplars where available.
- Forward exemplar references to tracing system (trace_id) for root cause linking.
- Expose health, self-metrics, and a debug endpoint to fetch current relabel rules.

Why not change existing producers:
Many integrations are third-party or live in customer-managed environments (Dedicated/Private). Centralizing transformation at ingestion avoids risky producer rollout windows and keeps SDKs simpler.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Router accepts OTLP and remote_write input in integration test and normalizes labels for three sample producers (gateway, runtime, cache).
2) Derived KPIs appear in our test Prometheus with correct values within 1% of offline golden calculation.
3) Cardinality control rules drop high-cardinality label combinations from raw metric stream while preserving SLO signals.
4) Exemplars are attached to histograms and linked to trace IDs for at least 90% of sampled high-latency requests.
5) Load test: 250k/sec sustained with <1s 99th-percentile ingestion latency across 3-node router cluster.
6) Console exposes a toggle to enable/disable derived KPI generation per dataset.
plan:
Phase 1 - Prototype (2 sprints):
- Implement OTLP input + minimal relabeler.
- Unit tests for label normalization rules and derived KPI formulas.
- E2E to Prometheus remote_write sink.

Phase 2 - Hardening & cardinality (2 sprints):
- Add cardinality guardrails (sample/drop rules, label value canonicalization).
- Implement exemplar forwarding to tracing.
- Integration tests with runtime team and gateway.

Phase 3 - Telemetry & rollout (1 sprint):
- Add internal metrics, dashboards for router health.
- Canary rollout to hosted ingestion path, monitor cost and SLO impact.
- Ramp to full traffic and document rollback/playbook.
migration_strategy: Start by enabling normalization-only mode for a subset of non-production tenants so we can compare derived KPIs to current dashboards. Then enable derived KPI computation for a small percentage (5%) of traffic with detailed logging. After validating accuracy and cost, iterate on cardinality rules before enabling production-wide. Use feature flags and GitOps-managed rule sets. Backward compatibility: raw incoming metrics are still forwarded unchanged to a cold path for compliance and debugging.
roll_out_plan:
1) Deploy router behind a feature-flagged collector cluster in staging.
2) Run 7-day validation comparing offline vs router-derived metrics.
3) Canary: route 5% of production ingestion through router for non-critical orgs.
4) After 72h and SLO stability, increase to 25% then 100% over two weeks.
5) Post-rollout: keep cold path for 30d and run nightly diffs for regression detection.
risks:
- Over-aggressive cardinality dropping might mask customer issues.
- Derived KPI computation bugs could lead to incorrect billing or SLO decisions.
- Memory blow-up under pathological label distributions.
- Tracing exemplar linkage may miss correlation if producers don't emit trace_id consistently.
